statements.text: In a Fox Business appearance, Donalds said parents and the state of Florida should lead decisions on regulating AI, and that protecting children and making sure parents know what their children are doing with AI tools is the top priority.

statements.text: A Florida Phoenix explainer on the stalled state AI Bill of Rights reported that Donalds thinks AI regulation should be left to the federal government, in line with President Trump's executive order on state AI laws.

gaps: Certification: no report found confirming that the Florida Elections Canvassing Commission met on Nov. 17, 2026 or certified either race; status is marked 'pending' for lack of confirmation, not because a delay was reported. County boards (e.g., Collier, Lee) certified by mid-November per WGCU.
Raw vote totals for both races were not found; percentages are unofficial (governor 50.1-48.7 per AP via Newsweek; Senate 50.9-48.0 per Ballotpedia).

Independents: the two major-party nominees took about 98.8% (governor) and 98.9% (Senate), so no independent drew notable support. Whether Jason Pizzo (NPA), who announced an independent run in 2025, appeared on the November ballot was not confirmed.

Primary figures: Donalds' GOP primary share differs by outlet (48.8%, 48.7%, 47.8%). Nixon's Democratic primary margin over Vindman (one AP-based report: 56.1% to 43.9%) could not be tied to a specific URL, and Moody's Republican primary opponents and vote share were not found.

Donalds: his House vote on the May 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill (which included a 10-year state AI-law moratorium) and on H.R. 9340 (Ratepayer Protection Act, passed 417-3) were not confirmed in search results. His AI stance shifts across reports (Feb. 2026 state/parent-led; April 2026 per Florida Phoenix federal; fall 2026 backing a Florida AI bill of rights). The exact dates of the Fox 13 and WPTV fall-campaign articles were not shown.

Moody: no AI- or data-center-specific bill sponsored or cosponsored as senator was found (her office says she cosponsors the Kids Online Safety Act, which is not AI-specific). Her vote to strip the AI moratorium is inferred from the 99-1 tally. No Senate-office statement on data centers was found; the original date and venue of the remarks summarized by Inside Climate News were not found. Reports say Moody and Nixon did not debate.
Nixon: no Florida House votes or bills on AI or data centers (e.g., the 2026 data center law SB 484 or DeSantis' AI Bill of Rights) were found. The date of the Newsweek interview is estimated.
Jolly: no AI-related record from his 2014-2017 House service was found. The attribution and date of his 'pump the brakes' quote come from search snippets (likely Floridian Press, July 22, 2026).

Polls: no Florida issue-priority poll fielded closer to the election (Sept.-Nov. 2026) was confirmed. Other Florida items whose dates or scope could not be confirmed: an AIF poll (property insurance 33%, inflation 21%, housing costs 11%), a Stetson poll (cost of living/inflation 39%, immigration 12%), a James Madison Institute poll (52% support new data centers, 29% oppose), and a Nov. 10, 2026 UnidosUS Latino voter poll (cost of living 59%, jobs/economy 35%). Whether AI was offered as an issue in the UNF March 2026 most-important-problem question is unknown. The publication date and margin of error of the Stetson September 2026 poll were not found.
The statewide polls are listed under both races; deduplicate if aggregating.
